2609.03774.title: Rethinking World Models for Safety-Critical Embodied Systems
2609.03774.paper_summary: World models have progressed from compact latent dynamics to generative, controllable, and interactive simulators of embodied environments. However, high predictive likelihood and visual fidelity do not necessarily ensure that a model preserves the evidence required for safe decision-making. This perspective identifies three structural mismatches in current world modeling: likelihood versus risk, prediction versus intervention, and finite-horizon prediction versus accumulated consequences. We propose the Risk-Informed World Model (RIWM) as a decision-centric research direction for safety-critical embodied systems. RIWM organizes world modeling around consequences, intervention, epistemic uncertainty, and recoverability, and integrates four interdependent capabilities: decision-relevant representation, counterfactual reasoning, safety-critical episodic memory, and runtime safety assurance. It distinguishes physical, social, and operational consequences while using epistemic uncertainty to qualify the evidence supporting action. We further discuss open challenges in identifying consequential futures, validating counterfactual reasoning, maintaining revisable safety memories, translating learned consequences into executable constraints, and determining when evidence is sufficient to act. This perspective argues that future world models should move beyond predicting likely futures toward identifying which futures matter, revising judgments through experience, and recognizing when to act, revise, sense, defer, or abstain.
2609.03774.paper_summary_zh: 世界模型已經從緊湊的潛在動態進展到生成的、可控的和互動的具身環境模擬器。<lb/>然而，高預測可能性和視覺真實性並不一定確保模型保留進行安全決策所需的證據。<lb/>這一觀點確定了當前世界建模中的三個結構不匹配：可能性與風險、預測與干預，以及有限時間預測與累積後果。<lb/>我們提出風險知情世界模型（RIWM），作為安全關鍵具身系統的以決策為中心的研究方向。<lb/>RIWM圍繞後果、干預、認知不確定性和可恢復性組織世界建模，並整合四個相互依賴的能力：與決策相關的表徵、反事實推理、安全關鍵的情節記憶和運行時安全保證。<lb/>它區分物理、社會和操作後果，同時利用認知不確定性來限定支持行動的證據。<lb/>我們進一步討論在識別後果未來、驗證反事實推理、維持可修訂的安全記憶、將學習到的後果轉化為可執行的約束，以及確定何時證據足以行動方面的開放挑戰。<lb/>這一觀點認為，未來的世界模型應該超越預測可能的未來，轉向識別哪些未來重要，通過經驗修正判斷，並認識何時行動、修正、感知、延遲或放棄。
